paragraphs: A model trained with several kinds of information can sometimes outperform a carefully tuned model trained with just one kind, even when the final task uses only one modality. This paper develops a theoretical explanation for that observation by studying generalization: how learning from available examples supports performance on unseen examples.

The analysis compares generalization bounds for multimodal and unimodal learning. It shows that the multimodal bound can be better by a factor of up to O(√n), where n is the number of training samples. This is a statement about theoretical bounds, rather than a guarantee that every multimodal model will achieve that improvement in measured accuracy.

The advantage depends on modalities having both connections and differences. Their relationship makes information transferable, while their heterogeneity supplies something beyond repeated versions of the same signal. The contribution is therefore a conditional account of why multiple modalities can help: their combination can support stronger generalization when they offer related but distinct information.
neurips-2023-a-theory-of-multimodal-lear.tldr: A theoretical framework shows how connected but heterogeneous modalities can improve generalization bounds over unimodal learning.

paragraphs: Detecting that two datasets differ does not identify which features caused the difference or how to repair them. This paper studies both questions together. Its motivating examples include malfunctioning sensors and errors in standardization or processing pipelines, where particular features become corrupted and produce a distribution shift between datasets.

The approach uses adversarial learning principles: several classifiers learn to distinguish observations from the two distributions, and information from those classifiers guides the search for corrupted features. The same information also supports corrections intended to remove the shift. This turns the ability to tell datasets apart into a tool for locating and repairing their differences.

The authors show that familiar supervised methods, including random forests and gradient boosting trees, can perform this work when combined with simple iterative heuristics. Their reported results outperform existing statistical and neural network approaches. The practical contribution is a way to move from a dataset-level warning toward feature-level diagnosis and correction using established classification tools.
neurips-2023-adversarial-learning-for-fe.tldr: Classifiers trained to distinguish datasets can guide iterative detection and correction of corrupted features that cause distribution shifts.

paragraphs: Designing an environment for many robots becomes difficult as its size grows, because the number of possible layouts increases exponentially. Earlier quality diversity approaches optimized relatively small warehouse environments directly. This paper instead optimizes generators, aiming to carry useful layout patterns from manageable training environments into much larger spaces.

The generators are neural cellular automata, and quality diversity algorithms train a collection of them on small environments. At test time, those learned generators produce environments of arbitrary size. The central change is the object being optimized: a reusable process for constructing layouts replaces the search for each individual large layout.

The authors find that generated environments retain consistent, regularized patterns across sizes. They report improved scalability in two multi-robot domains, with experiments reaching 2,350 robots. They also demonstrate that a single-agent reinforcement learning policy can operate in arbitrarily large environments with similar patterns. These findings connect scalable generation with behavioral reuse, while the concrete multi-robot evidence extends to the tested system sizes.
neurips-2023-arbitrarily-scalable-enviro.tldr: Optimizing neural cellular automata on small environments produces reusable generators that scale layouts to larger robot systems.

paragraphs: This paper addresses a theoretical question about neural network training: can gradient-based learning use fewer examples than kernel methods without requiring unusual changes to the optimization algorithm? It studies two-layer networks through a mean-field analysis of projected gradient flow, with network width allowed to grow polynomially with problem size.

The main result establishes a separation in sample requirements. With n = O(d^3.1) examples, where d is the input dimension, the analyzed network reaches a nontrivial error level in polynomial time. Kernel methods cannot reach that error level with sample counts much smaller than d^4 in the setting considered by the analysis.

The authors also connect the continuous-time result to an implementable update process. A corollary shows that projected gradient descent with a positive learning rate reaches low error in a polynomial number of iterations with the same sample complexity. Together, these results demonstrate a setting where the analyzed neural network training procedure exceeds what the neural tangent kernel perspective can achieve with comparable data.
neurips-2023-beyond-ntk-with-vanilla-gra.tldr: A mean-field analysis proves a sample-complexity advantage over kernel methods for polynomial-width networks trained with projected gradient methods.

paragraphs: Backdoor attacks poison training examples so that a model later misclassifies inputs carrying an attack pattern. Defense becomes especially difficult when the deployed model exposes only query access. This paper introduces Zero-shot Image Purification, or ZIP, which operates without access to model internals or prior knowledge of clean and poisoned samples.

ZIP first applies a linear transformation, such as blurring, to disrupt the backdoor pattern. Because this operation also removes useful image information, a pretrained diffusion model then reconstructs semantic content. The authors design a reverse generation process guided by the transformed image, allowing purification to remain tied to the image being processed.

The approach separates two competing needs: damaging the attack signal and recovering information needed for recognition. Its zero-shot design makes that process applicable under the stated black-box constraints. Across multiple datasets and attack types, the authors report better results than state-of-the-art backdoor defense baselines. The findings support image purification as a promising defense strategy for the evaluated attacks and models.
neurips-2023-black-box-backdoor-defense-.tldr: ZIP disrupts backdoor patterns with image transformations and uses guided diffusion to restore useful content without model access or example-specific prior knowledge.

paragraphs: Generating an image containing several user-specified subjects raises two linked problems: representing each subject efficiently and preventing subjects from interfering with one another. The paper addresses both, motivated by existing customization methods whose training costs rise and success rates fall as more subjects are included in a requested image.

For representation, the authors find that a subject token's text embedding can support arbitrary combinations without tuning the image model. They learn a residual added to a base embedding, shifting the generic subject representation toward the customized subject under different text conditions. This concentrates customization in the representation used to describe the subject.

For composition, the method uses a layout to specify where subjects should appear. It adjusts cross-attention maps to strengthen a target subject's signal within its region and suppress irrelevant subject signals there. This spatial separation reduces interference between subjects. Qualitative and quantitative experiments report improvements over state-of-the-art alternatives across several multi-subject customization settings, supporting the combination of compact subject representations and explicit spatial guidance.
neurips-2023-customizable-image-synthesi.tldr: Learned subject embeddings and layout-guided cross-attention improve the composition of multiple customized subjects in generated images.

paragraphs: Variational autoencoders provide a computationally efficient framework for modeling data, but Gaussian distribution assumptions can constrain their expressive power. This paper proposes a more flexible distributional model while retaining the framework's computational advantages. The aim is to broaden the kinds of continuous-variable distributions the model can fit.

The decoder uses an infinite mixture of asymmetric Laplace distributions. Rather than relying on a single Gaussian form, this construction provides general distribution-fitting capabilities for continuous variables. The authors also express the model as a particular nonparametric M-estimator for general quantile functions and theoretically establish its relationship to quantile estimation.

That connection gives the proposed decoder a statistical interpretation in terms of estimating positions throughout a distribution. The authors apply the method to synthetic data generation and report an advantage in how easily the level of data privacy can be adjusted. The contribution combines a broader decoder family, a theoretical account of its estimation behavior, and an application where controlling properties of generated data matters.
neurips-2023-distributional-learning-of-.tldr: A VAE decoder built from an infinite mixture of asymmetric Laplace distributions expands distributional flexibility and supports adjustable privacy in synthetic data generation.

paragraphs: Training several tasks together by minimizing their average loss can leave some tasks poorly optimized. Methods that directly manipulate task gradients seek a more balanced decrease in losses, but computing and storing every task's gradient costs time and memory proportional to the number of tasks. That overhead makes scaling more difficult.

Fast Adaptive Multitask Optimization, or FAMO, addresses this problem through dynamic task weighting. It adjusts how tasks contribute to optimization so that their losses decrease in a balanced way. The paper describes the method as using O(1) space and time, compared with the O(k) requirements of the gradient manipulation approaches under discussion, where k counts tasks.

Experiments cover both supervised multitask learning and reinforcement learning. The reported results match or exceed state-of-the-art gradient manipulation methods while substantially improving computational and memory efficiency. The significance is that balancing progress across tasks need not carry the same task-gradient handling costs as earlier methods, making this approach useful for pursuing more scalable multitask training.
neurips-2023-famo-fast-adaptive-multitas.tldr: FAMO dynamically balances task losses while reducing the time and memory costs associated with manipulating every task's gradient.

paragraphs: Many reinforcement learning methods discourage a new policy from moving too far from the previous one. They often measure that change using Kullback-Leibler divergence, which supplies a penalty for abrupt policy updates. This paper studies what happens when that standard measure is replaced by a more general Tsallis KL divergence.

The generalized divergence depends on a parameter q through the q-logarithm. Setting q to 1 recovers ordinary KL divergence, while values above 1 introduce additional choices. The authors characterize the kinds of policies learned with this regularization and discuss circumstances in which those additional choices could be beneficial.

To make the idea practical, they extend Munchausen Value Iteration, yielding a family called MVI(q). This keeps the investigation tied to an algorithm that already incorporates KL regularization simply. Across 35 Atari games, the generalized method produces significant improvements over the standard q = 1 version. The findings support changing the form of policy regularization as a useful algorithmic choice, with benefits demonstrated in the evaluated games.
neurips-2023-general-munchausen-reinforc.tldr: Generalizing Munchausen Value Iteration with Tsallis KL regularization improves reported performance over standard MVI across 35 Atari games.

paragraphs: Neural operators learn mappings between spaces of functions. This paper investigates when such mappings are injective, meaning distinct inputs remain distinguishable, and surjective, meaning every output in the target space is reachable. These properties matter for inversion because they correspond to uniqueness and existence of solutions.

The authors give sharp injectivity conditions for ReLU layers built with linear neural operators, followed by sufficient conditions for layers with pointwise bijective activations. Infinite-rank operators require more subtle reasoning than finite-rank ones, addressed using Fredholm theory. They also prove universal approximation results for their injective operators and show that finite-rank network implementations preserve injectivity.

The analysis then extends to subnetworks with potentially many layers, supplying general conditions for injectivity and surjectivity and an exact inversion through a linearization. These conclusions apply under the conditions developed in the paper. The authors identify possible applications in inverse problems and Bayesian uncertainty quantification, where preserving these mapping properties could support solution guarantees and likelihood estimation.
neurips-2023-globally-injective-and-bije.tldr: The paper establishes conditions for injective and surjective neural operators, including preservation of injectivity in finite-rank network implementations.

paragraphs: Neural denoisers are widely useful, but their success is difficult to explain theoretically. This paper studies the actual functions represented by shallow ReLU denoisers under a specific constraint: they fit the training data with zero loss while minimizing the squared norm of their weights. The focus is the resulting function's shape.

For one-dimensional data, the authors derive an explicit formula and show that the denoiser contracts inputs toward clean training points. They also prove better generalization than the empirical minimum mean-square-error estimator at low noise levels. That noise qualification is part of the result, rather than a claim of superiority across all denoising conditions.

For higher-dimensional data, explicit formulas follow under particular geometric assumptions, including low-dimensional subspaces, unions of one-sided rays, and several simplex configurations. The functions combine simple rank-one, piecewise-linear interpolations aligned with edges or faces linking training samples. Experiments on synthetic data and real images verify the alignment phenomenon, connecting the theoretical descriptions to observed denoiser behavior.
neurips-2023-how-do-minimum-norm-shallow.tldr: Under interpolation and minimum-weight-norm constraints, shallow ReLU denoisers admit explicit descriptions tied to the geometry of clean training samples.

paragraphs: Image retrieval across domains requires representations that retain relevant content despite changes in domain-specific appearance. This paper studies unsupervised domain adaptive hashing, transferring knowledge from a source with abundant labels to a target with scarce labels. Its concern is that domain differences can contaminate the hash codes used for retrieval.

The proposed IDEA model separates each image into features intended to represent label information and features intended to represent domain information. It generates discriminative hash codes from the label-related features, using consistency learning across source and target domains. This decomposition gives the model an explicit way to distinguish retrieval-relevant information from domain-associated variation.

IDEA also uses a generative model to create synthetic samples that simulate interventions on non-causal, domain-related effects. Training seeks to reduce the influence of those effects on the codes. Benchmark experiments report better performance than a range of competitive baselines. The findings support combining feature separation and synthetic interventions to make cross-domain retrieval depend less on domain-specific image properties.
neurips-2023-idea-an-invariant-perspecti.tldr: IDEA separates label-related and domain-related features, then uses synthetic interventions to learn more domain-invariant image retrieval codes.

paragraphs: Neural networks can reconstruct signals accurately while remaining sensitive to worst-case changes in their inputs. This paper asks whether a simple training technique can improve that robustness for inverse problems. The technique, called jittering, adds isotropic Gaussian noise during training, spreading random perturbations equally across directions.

The theoretical analysis focuses on linear denoising. The authors characterize the optimal estimator against worst-case perturbations measured in the ℓ2 norm and show that jittering produces optimal robust denoisers in this setting. This establishes a precise connection between training with random noise and protection against deliberately unfavorable perturbations.

Experiments train U-nets for natural image denoising, deconvolution, and accelerated MRI reconstruction. Jittering substantially improves worst-case robustness, but the results also show that it can be suboptimal beyond denoising. The distinction matters: the linear denoising guarantee does not automatically extend to every inverse problem. The findings additionally suggest that slight noise already present in real training data can provide some robustness benefit.
neurips-2023-learning-provably-robust-es.tldr: Gaussian training noise yields optimal robust estimators for linear denoising and improves empirical robustness in several inverse problems, though it can be suboptimal beyond denoising.

paragraphs: Tone mapping converts high dynamic range images into lower dynamic range representations. Three-dimensional lookup tables offer a useful balance of enhancement quality and efficiency, but their pixel-value-based transformations miss local context. This paper addresses that weakness by combining global tone adjustment with local edge processing in one learned system.

The method uses Laplacian pyramid decomposition to separate image information by frequency. Image-adaptive lookup tables adjust the low-frequency image, while local Laplacian filters refine edges in higher-frequency components. Pyramid reconstruction then brings those components together, allowing the method to handle broad tonal structure and fine detail through complementary operations.

Conventional local Laplacian filters rely on manually chosen parameters and fixed implementations. Here, a lightweight network progressively learns parameter maps from annotated examples, making the local processing adaptive within end-to-end training. Experiments on two benchmark datasets report favorable performance against state-of-the-art methods. The contribution is a learned integration of global tone manipulation and local detail preservation, organized around the different information carried at different image frequencies.
neurips-2023-lookup-table-meets-local-la.tldr: A learned pyramid reconstruction method combines adaptive lookup tables for global tone with local Laplacian filters for edge preservation.

paragraphs: Increasing a Vision Transformer's depth does not automatically improve its performance. The authors identify degradation in deeper layers during masked image modeling pretraining and introduce Masked Image Residual Learning, or MIRL, to ease optimization. Its central change is to make deeper layers learn to recover the masked image's residual.

The experiments show that MIRL substantially reduces the degradation problem and allows deeper networks to benefit from added depth. The authors construct ViT-S-54 and ViT-B-48, which are respectively 4.5 and 2 times deeper than ViT-Base and ViT-Large while matching their corresponding levels of computational complexity. These comparisons explore depth without simply increasing computational demands proportionally.

ViT-S-54 matches ViT-Large's performance at roughly one-third of its stated computational cost, while ViT-B-48 reaches 86.2% ImageNet top-1 accuracy. The paper also reports strong transfer to object detection and semantic segmentation, alongside competitive performance with less pretraining time. Together, the results support residual-based pretraining as a practical way to make greater transformer depth useful.
neurips-2023-masked-image-residual-learn.tldr: MIRL changes deeper Vision Transformer layers' pretraining target to image residuals, reducing degradation and enabling useful gains from added depth.

paragraphs: Text-to-image diffusion models depend on initial random seeds, but combining those seeds through familiar geometric operations can work poorly. This paper studies interpolation and centroid construction in seed space. Its key observation is that current training procedures expose diffusion models to inputs whose norms occupy a narrow range.

The authors build an interpolation method that accounts for this norm-based prior. They show that it defines a non-Euclidean metric, giving seed manipulation a geometry informed by the inputs encountered during training. They also supply a simple, efficient approximation algorithm and use the interpolation procedure to define centroids among multiple seeds.

The proposed operations significantly improve the generation of images containing rare concepts. The authors report state-of-the-art results on few-shot and long-tail benchmarks, with improvements in generation speed, image quality, and semantic content over prior approaches. The findings show that the geometry chosen for manipulating initial seeds can have practical consequences for generation, particularly when the target concepts are supported by few examples.
neurips-2023-norm-guided-latent-space-ex.tldr: Norm-aware interpolation and centroid construction in diffusion seed space improve rare-concept generation and reported few-shot and long-tail performance.

paragraphs: Recognizing actions becomes harder when objects obscure the action in a video. This paper introduces five benchmarks covering controlled static and moving occlusions, occluders with realistic motion, and real-world occlusion scenarios. The evaluations confirm that increasing obstruction hurts existing models and that static and moving occluders produce different behaviors.

The authors observe that transformers can outperform convolutional models even when those models received occlusion augmentation during training. Adding capsule-like symbolic components enables binding to previously unseen occluders. They also observe groups of agreeing representations, described as islands of agreement, without instance-level supervision, distillation, or contrastive objectives. These observations motivate training recipes for grouping and separating visual information.

Models using those recipes outperform existing action detectors under occlusion, with reported vMAP improvements of 32.3% on O-UCF, 32.7% on O-JHMDB, and 2.6% on Real-OUCF. The work contributes both evaluation resources and training methods. Its findings connect observed representation behavior to improved detection when relevant action content is partially hidden.
neurips-2023-on-occlusions-in-video-acti.tldr: Five occlusion benchmarks reveal model behaviors that motivate training recipes improving video action detection under partial obstruction.

paragraphs: CART fits decision trees through a sequence of greedy splits, making a locally attractive choice at each stage. This paper studies how quickly its prediction error decreases in regression. The analysis assumes a sufficient impurity decrease condition, which supplies a mathematical requirement on the improvement available through splitting.

Under that condition, the authors prove an upper bound on CART's prediction error that improves an earlier result based on a similar assumption. They also provide examples showing that the new bound cannot generally be tightened by more than a constant or logarithmic factor. This makes the result informative about both achievable guarantees and their remaining room for improvement.

The paper then makes the assumption easier to assess by deriving sufficient conditions for it. In particular, additive models can satisfy the requirement when their component functions obey a locally reverse Poincare inequality. Examples from familiar nonparametric function classes illustrate its usefulness. The contribution therefore combines a sharper conditional error bound with ways to recognize settings where that bound applies.
neurips-2023-on-the-convergence-of-cart-.tldr: The paper sharpens CART regression error bounds under sufficient impurity decrease and provides conditions for checking when that assumption holds.

paragraphs: Gradient-based meta-learning can learn how an optimization process updates its parameters. This paper connects that idea to convex optimization, beginning with the observation that gradient descent with momentum is a special case of meta-gradients. That connection allows familiar optimization tools to clarify what learning an update rule can accomplish.

Building on optimization results, the authors prove convergence rates for meta-learning in a single-task setting. They distinguish a constant-factor speed improvement from acceleration of the convergence rate. A meta-learned update rule can provide the former, but learning such a rule alone is insufficient for the latter in the analysis.

The missing ingredient is some form of optimism, which the paper shows can be captured through the Bootstrapped Meta-Gradient method. This gives a theoretical interpretation of that method's mechanics and explains why the structure of the meta-learning procedure matters. The result concerns the analyzed single-task setting and separates faster execution of a convergence pattern from a stronger improvement in how convergence scales.
neurips-2023-optimistic-meta-gradients-d.tldr: A single-task convergence analysis shows that meta-learned updates can offer constant-factor gains, while acceleration requires an additional form of optimism.

paragraphs: Penalizing neural network parameter norms can influence the shape of the learned function, but that relationship is not always transparent. This paper analyzes networks with one hidden ReLU layer and one-dimensional inputs. It asks how including bias parameters in the penalty changes the minimum-norm function that exactly fits the data.

The authors express the norm needed to represent a function through the total variation of its second derivative, weighted by √(1+x²). For these piecewise-linear functions, changes in slope are the relevant geometric events. The weighting factor disappears when biases are excluded from regularization, so the two penalties impose meaningfully different preferences on function shape.

The paper shows that the extra weighting enforces uniqueness and sparsity of the minimum-norm interpolator, with sparsity measured by the number of kinks. Omitting bias penalties permits non-sparse solutions. Within the studied setting, explicitly or implicitly regularizing biases therefore affects more than parameter size: it determines whether the preferred interpolating function has a sparse set of slope changes.
neurips-2023-penalising-the-biases-in-no.tldr: For one-hidden-layer ReLU networks on one-dimensional data, penalizing biases enforces a unique minimum-norm interpolator with sparse slope changes.

paragraphs: Machine learning systems that analyze programs depend on how code is represented. This paper argues that earlier representations lose useful information about numbers, aggregate data structures, and variables. PERFOGRAPH addresses those gaps with a graph representation designed to retain more of the dependencies and semantics relevant to program analysis.

The representation introduces nodes and edges for numerical information and aggregate data structures. An adapted embedding method also incorporates numerical awareness. These changes give learning methods access to information that previous representations handled inadequately, with intended uses including performance optimization, program analysis, and discovery of opportunities for parallel execution.

In the Device Mapping challenge, the authors report state-of-the-art results and error-rate reductions of 7.4% on the AMD dataset and 10% on the NVIDIA dataset. They also report new leading results for parallelism discovery and prediction of NUMA and prefetcher configurations. The findings support improving the program representation itself as a route to better learning-based decisions across several performance-related tasks.
neurips-2023-perfograph-a-numerical-awar.tldr: PERFOGRAPH adds numerical and aggregate-structure information to program graphs, improving reported results across several program performance tasks.

paragraphs: Autonomous driving systems must predict nearby participants' future motion within onboard computing constraints. Agent-centric methods can predict accurately, but their computational overhead scales poorly as the number of participants grows. This paper develops a transformer framework intended to preserve strong prediction performance while sharing and reusing more scene information.

The core attention mechanism, KNARPE, combines nearest-neighbor attention with relative pose encoding so transformers can use pairwise-relative representations. The authors build the Heterogeneous Polyline Transformer with Relative pose encoding, or HPTR, around it. Its hierarchy supports asynchronous token updates during online inference, sharing context across agents and reusing context that has not changed.

The authors report efficiency comparable to scene-centric methods and performance comparable to state-of-the-art agent-centric methods. On Waymo and Argoverse-2, HPTR achieves superior results among end-to-end approaches that avoid expensive post-processing and model ensembles. The contribution links representation design with computation reuse, addressing the repeated processing that makes multi-agent motion prediction difficult to scale in deployment.
neurips-2023-real-time-motion-prediction.tldr: HPTR combines relative-pose attention with shared, reusable context to make multi-agent motion prediction efficient while retaining strong benchmark performance.

paragraphs: Residual networks use skip connections, but the mechanisms behind their effectiveness remain incompletely understood. This paper examines classification models by locally linearizing residual blocks through their Jacobians and analyzing singular value decompositions. Those measurements reveal a recurring geometric pattern the authors call Residual Alignment.

For a given input, intermediate representations lie approximately along an evenly spaced line. Leading left and right singular vectors align within residual Jacobians and across depths, while leading singular values scale inversely with depth. In fully connected ResNets, the residual Jacobians have rank at most equal to the number of classes. Together, these properties describe coordinated transformations across layers.

The pattern consistently appears in well-generalizing models across the tested architectures, sizes, class counts, and datasets, but disappears when skip connections are removed. The authors also prove it in a mathematical model they introduce. Their findings describe a rigid geometry through intermediate layers, followed by Neural Collapse at the final layer, offering empirical and theoretical evidence about how residual branches cooperate.
neurips-2023-residual-alignment-uncoveri.tldr: Measurements reveal coordinated residual transformations and nearly linear representation paths in tested well-generalizing ResNets, with supporting proof in a proposed mathematical model.

paragraphs: Area convexity is an optimization tool developed for problems with challenging ℓ∞ geometry. This paper clarifies its relationship to conventional analyses of extragradient methods. It also improves the solvers needed for internal subproblems, using relative smoothness as the organizing principle for those algorithmic changes.

These tools produce a first-order algorithm for box-simplex games, which express ℓ∞ regression as a primal-dual problem. For a d by n matrix with bounded rows, the algorithm uses O(log d · ε⁻¹) matrix-vector queries, where ε specifies the desired accuracy. The bounded-row assumption is part of the stated setting for this complexity result.

The improved solver yields better complexity bounds for approximate maximum flow, optimal transport, minimum mean cycle, and other combinatorial optimization problems. The authors also develop a near-linear-time method for a matrix generalization related to semidefinite programs used in robust statistics and numerical linear algebra. The contribution connects a clearer understanding of an optimization technique with faster algorithms for several families of problems.
neurips-2023-revisiting-area-convexity-f.tldr: A refined analysis of area convexity yields faster box-simplex game solvers and a near-linear-time algorithm for a related matrix generalization.

paragraphs: Larger vision models trained on larger datasets have improved accuracy, but that does not establish whether their internal computations are easier to understand. This paper tests that question using a psychophysical evaluation of one form of mechanistic interpretability. The study covers nine models and uses human responses to assess interpretability.

The authors find no improvement associated with either model size or training dataset size on the measure they study. None of the investigated state-of-the-art models is easier to interpret than GoogLeNet. More recent architectures appear even less interpretable, suggesting a possible regression rather than a corresponding interpretability benefit from greater predictive performance.

The paper releases more than 130,000 human responses covering 767 units across the nine models. This resource supports research into automated interpretability evaluation, which could eventually help optimize interpretability directly. The findings motivate architecture and evaluation methods that explicitly target understandability, while remaining specific to the models and form of interpretability examined in the study.
neurips-2023-scale-alone-does-not-improv.tldr: A human evaluation of nine vision models finds no scaling benefit for the studied form of mechanistic interpretability.
